summary: Coos County, OR: 50-ft wooden live-in tower built 1934-36 near Sitkum; destroyed or dismantled in 1964, site auctioned 1972; no source describes it today.

facts.status_note: Destroyed in 1964 per firelookout.com; dismantled that year per Forest Lookouts. No source describes the site today

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com dates the 50-foot tower to 1935; Forest Lookouts reports framework finished in October 1934 and a new tower and lookout house in April 1936. The story gives the range 1934-36 and keeps each date as its own event.
Firelookout.com says destroyed; Forest Lookouts says the tower and cab were dismantled. Both date the event to 1964, so both are kept as separate events and the story reports the disagreement.

notes_for_editor: Brewster Rock has two detailed local histories that agree on the 1934 start and the 1964 end but differ on the completion date (1935 vs 1934 framework and 1936 new tower) and on whether the tower was destroyed or dismantled. Forest Lookouts also carries a 1942 USGS station description and a 1944 Aircraft Warning Service note ('George 7-9') that says the state kept the site afterwards; the page does not clearly tie that station to this lookout, so it is left out of the story. The brief's height (15.2 m) matches the 50-foot figure in both sources. No current source was found on the site's condition, owner or public access; a county or state land record search and a 1972 auction notice would be the next steps. No corrections proposed.
